goal.request: Prevent centered-frontal pose normalization by representing visible human orientation at independent degrees of freedom, without installing the motivating direction, placement, person, clothing, or camera angle as a default.

evidence.claim: The motivating source is near the frame center but does not read as axially neutral: head, torso, shoulder, side-visibility, and depth cues jointly create an asymmetric source-relative pose and direction.
The delivered motivating render stacks the face, neck, torso, and bilateral hair mass close to the central vertical axis and reads more frontal and symmetric than the source.

evidence.claim: The prior plan made frame placement invariant as centered, treated body orientation as one flexible coarse field, treated shoulder line as one non-material coarse field, and inferred near-frontal azimuth partly from both eyes and shoulders being visible. The prompt then emitted centered placement and an upright torso before local face, hair, and garment controls.

The v2 validator rejects the prior plan for a missing schema version, missing structured cues and neutralization checks, three legacy coarse human-pose dimensions, and nine uncovered decomposed pose axes.

All 172 reverse-image-prompt tests pass with 20 skips. Module validation passes for 37 modules at 16940 runtime words, 3800 Tier-0 words, and 0.0014 duplicate ratio; generated metadata and compiled profiles are current, Python compilation passes, and the diff has no whitespace errors.

evidence.claim: Regression tests cover independent yaw, pitch, roll, lateral-offset, shoulder-slope, shoulder-depth, and attention decisions; cue ownership and confounders; material and non-material neutralization; and direction-neutral causal pairs where mirrored oblique poses and truly frontal head-body alignment are both valid.

perceptual_contract.primary_success_condition: Frame placement cannot silently neutralize an independently material human pose; every visible pose degree of freedom is either source-supported and actuated once or explicitly bounded as non-emitted.

invariants.statement: Centered, offset, or edge placement controls frame position only and never implies frontal, oblique, aligned, or opposed orientation.
Torso, head-to-body, shoulder, and attention relations remain independently decidable instead of collapsing into coarse pose labels.
Replacing the observed relation with neutral axial alignment is an explicit counterfactual whose material visible changes require at least one invariant pose control.
The rules accept either oblique direction, mirrored evidence, and genuinely frontal alignment without preferring the motivating value.

flexible_dimensions: whether each decomposed axis is invariant or non-emitted
subject identity, appearance, garment, background, and medium
camera and pose split when source evidence cannot identify it

mismatches.axis: human pose relative to frame and camera
mismatches.source_state: Near-center placement coexists with an asymmetric head, torso, shoulder, and depth reading.
mismatches.render_state: The subject reads centered, frontal, and axially stacked.

mismatches.axis: independent human pose degrees of freedom
mismatches.source_state: Several part relations may remain material even when garments or hair obscure one landmark.
mismatches.render_state: The prior plan made coarse body orientation flexible and coarse shoulder line non-material, allowing local appearance inventory to settle into a neutral pose.

hypotheses.statement: Coarse body, head-body, and shoulder fields allow one visible subaxis to hide unexamined yaw, roll, lateral-offset, slope, or depth-order evidence.
hypotheses.falsifier: Independent held-out audits show that coarse dispositions always preserve every material subaxis and reject missing ones.

hypotheses.statement: An early centered-placement instruction plus weak or non-emitted orientation controls creates a neutral axial attractor even though placement and pose are logically independent.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched repeated renders preserve source-relative obliqueness when only centered placement is strong and material pose relations remain omitted.

hypotheses.statement: Face, hair, and garment inventory can reinforce bilateral symmetry or substitute for pose when the material head/torso/shoulder relation is absent or ordered too late.
hypotheses.falsifier: Held-out prompt and render pairs show no normalization difference when material pose is actuated before versus omitted beneath local appearance inventory.

intervention.general_rule: Use a versioned, direction-neutral spatial ledger that decomposes human pose axes, links each decision to subject-owned source cues and confounders, requires a neutral-alignment counterfactual, separates placement from orientation, and emits material pose before dependent appearance inventory.
intervention.generalization_basis: The implementation encodes degrees of freedom, evidence families, counterfactual outcomes, and ownership rather than any target direction, angle, coordinate, body, garment, face type, or generator workaround. Causal-pair tests accept mirrored obliqueness and true frontal alignment equally.

decision.rationale: The package now rejects the prior omission pattern and covers independent pose axes, cue/confounder provenance, neutralization, prompt order, and direction-neutral counterexamples. No post-intervention prompt or render was produced in this apply-only turn, so prompt behavior and pixel fidelity remain unscored and the change is not promoted beyond structural implementation.
